issues.description: The problem statement and UML define ExcellenceLand.excellentEnough as a boolean and require public getters for all attributes. In the solution, the getter is implemented as public String isExcellentEnough() returning "yes"/"no" instead of a boolean. This deviates from the specified attribute type and the expected boolean getter signature, which can confuse students about the correct getter return type and break code/tests expecting a boolean.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution's getter to match the UML and problem statement: implement public boolean isExcellentEnough() that returns the boolean attribute excellentEnough. If a human-readable string is desired, provide an additional method (e.g., getExcellentEnoughAsString()) but keep the boolean getter for correctness.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) defines ExcellenceLand.excellentEnough as a boolean attribute and requires public getters for all attributes (so students expect a boolean getter, typically isExcellentEnough() returning boolean). In the provided solution the method isExcellentEnough() exists but returns a String ("yes"/"no") instead of the boolean field. This mismatches the problem/specification representation of the same conceptual entity and can confuse students about the expected getter signature and type.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the UML/problem statement: change the solution method to a boolean getter that returns the field, e.g. public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; }. If a String representation is desired, add a separate method (e.g. public String getExcellentEnoughAsString()) instead of changing the boolean getter.
